name: Greece
snapshot: A fraud scandal over EU farm subsidies, centred on Crete, led to indictments of lawmakers from Mitsotakis's own party and dented his government.
culture: Greece is the cradle of Western philosophy, democracy and theatre, and the Acropolis remains its emblem. The Orthodox Church shapes holidays, with Easter the biggest. Islands like Santorini and Mykonos draw millions of visitors. Rebetiko, the "Greek blues" born in refugee communities, and bouzouki music fill tavernas.
society: The 2010s debt crisis cost Greece a quarter of its economy and sent hundreds of thousands of young people abroad. Growth has returned and debt is falling. Tourism is about a fifth of GDP. The 2023 Tempi rail crash, which killed 57, sparked the largest protests in years over corruption and state failure.
situation: On 28 February 2023, a passenger train and a freight train collided head-on at Tempi in central Greece, killing 57 people, many of them students heading home from carnival. Investigations found that basic safety systems on the line had never been finished despite years of EU funding. Three years later, Tempi is still the centre of Greek politics, and in 2026 a second scandal joined it.

That one is about farm subsidies. European prosecutors found that fraudsters, many in Crete, had claimed EU money for land they did not own and animals that did not exist, with help from officials at the payments agency OPEKEPE. In July the European Public Prosecutor indicted four lawmakers from Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis's New Democracy party, including its former political secretary (AFP via Neos Kosmos). Mitsotakis, whose family has dominated Cretan politics for a century, abolished the agency, moved its work to the tax authority and said the fraud predated him, while farmers blocked highways and airports over late payments. Polls in the winter put the government's satisfaction rating at about 27 percent; the most admired public figure was Maria Karystianou, the mother of a Tempi victim who has led the fight for accountability and is weighing her own party (To Vima). New Democracy still leads every poll because the opposition is fractured, and Mitsotakis has ruled out autumn elections. The Greek story is not economic collapse anymore. It is a country that recovered from its debt crisis and now asks whether its state can be trusted.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 300-seat Hellenic Parliament, elected by a system that gives the winning party bonus seats; the president, elected by parliament, is largely ceremonial.
holders: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis (New Democracy), in office since 2019.
